CHILLI_ANTHRACNOSE.inspect.1: Look at the tips of tender twigs for drying that runs from the tip downwards.
CHILLI_ANTHRACNOSE.inspect.2: Check ripe fruits for small round spots and for dark patches with a sharp black or straw-coloured edge.
CHILLI_ANTHRACNOSE.inspect.3: Watch the crop closely once flowering starts — infection usually begins when the crop is in flower.
CHILLI_ANTHRACNOSE.inspect.4: The disease shows up after the rains stop, when dew stays on the plants for long periods. Inspect on those days.
CHILLI_ANTHRACNOSE.nextStep.1: Collect and remove affected fruits and dried twigs from the field.
CHILLI_ANTHRACNOSE.nextStep.2: Use only disease-free seed next season — this disease is carried on seed.
CHILLI_ANTHRACNOSE.nextStep.3: Chemical sprays are published for this disease, but this app does not give doses. Contact your nearest KVK, or call the Kisan Call Centre on 1800-180-1551, before spraying anything.
CHILLI_ANTHRACNOSE.prevention.2: Remove affected fruits and dried twigs from the field instead of leaving them lying.
CHILLI_ANTHRACNOSE.symptom.1: Tender twigs die back from the tip downwards; the branches and stem then dry and wither.
CHILLI_ANTHRACNOSE.symptom.2: Flowers drop heavily. The flower stalk shrivels and dries, and the drying spreads from the flower stalk into the stem.
CHILLI_ANTHRACNOSE.symptom.3: Ripe fruits show small round spots at first, which spread into oblong black-green patches with a clear black or straw-coloured edge.
CHILLI_ANTHRACNOSE.symptom.4: Badly affected fruits turn straw-coloured, shrivel and dry up, and are less pungent. Affected plants carry few fruits and of low quality.
CHILLI_BACTERIAL_SPOT.inspect.1: Hold a leaf up to the light and look for small greasy dark spots whose centres have turned lighter with a dark ring around them.
CHILLI_BACTERIAL_SPOT.inspect.2: Check the stems and leaf stalks for canker-like rough growths and for wilting branches.
CHILLI_BACTERIAL_SPOT.inspect.3: Check fruits for raised water-soaked spots with a pale yellow edge.
CHILLI_BACTERIAL_SPOT.nextStep.1: Keep the field clean — remove affected plants and plant debris.
CHILLI_BACTERIAL_SPOT.nextStep.2: Take seed only from disease-free plants for the next crop.
CHILLI_BACTERIAL_SPOT.nextStep.3: Chemical sprays are published for this disease, but this app does not give doses. Contact your nearest KVK, or call the Kisan Call Centre on 1800-180-1551.
CHILLI_BACTERIAL_SPOT.prevention.1: Obtain seed only from disease-free plants.
CHILLI_BACTERIAL_SPOT.prevention.2: Keep the field clean — field sanitation matters for this disease.
CHILLI_BACTERIAL_SPOT.symptom.1: Leaves show small round or irregular dark brown to black greasy spots.
CHILLI_BACTERIAL_SPOT.symptom.2: As the spots grow, the centre becomes lighter with a dark band of tissue around it, and the spots join into irregular patches.
CHILLI_BACTERIAL_SPOT.symptom.3: Badly affected leaves turn yellow and fall off.
CHILLI_BACTERIAL_SPOT.symptom.4: Leaf stalks and stems are also affected; stem infection makes canker-like rough growths and the branches wilt.
CHILLI_BACTERIAL_SPOT.symptom.5: Fruits show round, raised, water-soaked spots with a pale yellow border, which later turn brown and sink in the centre.
CHILLI_CERCOSPORA_LEAF_SPOT.inspect.1: Look for round brown spots with a pale grey centre, and check whether they have reached about 1 cm across.
CHILLI_CERCOSPORA_LEAF_SPOT.inspect.2: Check stems, leaf stalks and pods for oval lesions with grey centres.
CHILLI_CERCOSPORA_LEAF_SPOT.inspect.3: Inspect after humid, drizzly or windy weather, which helps this disease develop and spread.
CHILLI_CERCOSPORA_LEAF_SPOT.nextStep.1: Remove and destroy infected crop debris — the fungus survives in it.
CHILLI_CERCOSPORA_LEAF_SPOT.nextStep.2: Chemical sprays are published for this disease, but this app does not give doses. Contact your nearest KVK, or call the Kisan Call Centre on 1800-180-1551.
CHILLI_CERCOSPORA_LEAF_SPOT.prevention.1: Remove and destroy infected crop debris after harvest, because the fungus survives in it.
CHILLI_CERCOSPORA_LEAF_SPOT.symptom.1: Leaf spots are brown and round, with small to large light grey centres and dark brown edges.
CHILLI_CERCOSPORA_LEAF_SPOT.symptom.2: Spots may grow to 1 cm or more across, and sometimes join together.
CHILLI_CERCOSPORA_LEAF_SPOT.symptom.3: Stem, leaf-stalk and pod lesions also have light grey centres with dark borders, but they are usually oval rather than round.
CHILLI_CERCOSPORA_LEAF_SPOT.symptom.4: Badly infected leaves fall off early, which reduces yield.
CHILLI_HEALTHY.inspect.1: No disease signs were found in this check. Keep looking at the crop regularly.
CHILLI_HEALTHY.inspect.2: Turn leaves over and look at the underside — powdery mildew and bacterial leaf spot both show there first.
CHILLI_HEALTHY.inspect.3: Look more closely once flowering begins, and again after the rains stop when dew stays on the plants.
CHILLI_HEALTHY.prevention.2: Keep the field clean and remove crop debris.
CHILLI_HEALTHY.prevention.3: Raise the nursery under a net house or a cover, to protect seedlings from insects that carry viruses.
CHILLI_HEALTHY.prevention.4: Place yellow sticky traps in the field to watch for whitefly.
CHILLI_HEALTHY.prevention.6: Raise two rows of maize or sorghum as a barrier crop for every five rows of chilli.
CHILLI_LEAF_CURL_VIRUS.inspect.1: Compare new leaves with older ones lower down — affected leaves are much smaller.
CHILLI_LEAF_CURL_VIRUS.inspect.2: Look for upward cupping of the leaf margins and for yellowing between the veins.
CHILLI_LEAF_CURL_VIRUS.inspect.3: Check the underside of leaves for whitefly, which carries this virus.
CHILLI_LEAF_CURL_VIRUS.nextStep.1: Uproot infected plants and burn or bury them, so the virus does not spread further.
CHILLI_LEAF_CURL_VIRUS.nextStep.2: There is no cure for most virus diseases — management is cultural and aimed at the insect that carries it. Contact your nearest KVK, or call the Kisan Call Centre on 1800-180-1551, for local guidance. This app does not give doses.
CHILLI_LEAF_CURL_VIRUS.prevention.2: Cover nursery beds with nylon net or straw to protect the seedlings.
CHILLI_LEAF_CURL_VIRUS.prevention.3: Place yellow sticky traps in the field to watch for whitefly.
CHILLI_LEAF_CURL_VIRUS.prevention.5: Raise two to three rows of maize or sorghum as a border crop around the field.
CHILLI_LEAF_CURL_VIRUS.prevention.6: Avoid growing chilli after chilli in the same field year after year.
CHILLI_LEAF_CURL_VIRUS.symptom.1: Leaves curl towards the midrib and become deformed; the leaf margins curl upward, giving a cup-like appearance.
CHILLI_LEAF_CURL_VIRUS.symptom.2: Leaves are much smaller than normal and show yellowing between the veins.
CHILLI_LEAF_CURL_VIRUS.symptom.3: The plant is stunted, because the internodes are shortened.
CHILLI_LEAF_CURL_VIRUS.symptom.4: Flower buds drop before reaching full size, and the anthers carry no pollen.
CHILLI_NUTRIENT_DEFICIENCY.inspect.1: Note which leaves are affected — the older lower leaves, or the newest leaves at the top. The pattern is different for different nutrients.
CHILLI_NUTRIENT_DEFICIENCY.inspect.2: Note whether the whole leaf is pale, only the edges are burned, or only the area between the veins has yellowed.
CHILLI_NUTRIENT_DEFICIENCY.inspect.3: A photograph cannot say which nutrient is short. The same look can come from more than one nutrient, and insect or disease damage can look like a deficiency.
CHILLI_NUTRIENT_DEFICIENCY.nextStep.1: Get a soil test, and a plant test if you can. What you see on the leaf should only be used alongside soil and plant analysis, not instead of it.
CHILLI_NUTRIENT_DEFICIENCY.nextStep.2: Take an affected plant or a clear photo to your nearest KVK, or call the Kisan Call Centre on 1800-180-1551. This app does not give fertilizer doses.
CHILLI_NUTRIENT_DEFICIENCY.prevention.1: Test the soil before the season and plan nutrient application from the test result, rather than waiting for symptoms — by the time symptoms appear, yield has usually already been lost.
CHILLI_NUTRIENT_DEFICIENCY.symptom.1: Leaves are light green or yellow, the plant grows slowly and stays small.
CHILLI_NUTRIENT_DEFICIENCY.symptom.2: When nitrogen is short, the older lower leaves turn yellow first and may later turn brown and die.
CHILLI_NUTRIENT_DEFICIENCY.symptom.3: When potassium is short, the edges of the older leaves look burned or scorched.
CHILLI_NUTRIENT_DEFICIENCY.symptom.4: Older leaves may also show yellowing between the veins, or a purple colour, especially on the underside.
CHILLI_POWDERY_MILDEW.inspect.1: Turn the leaves over — the powdery growth is on the underside, not on the top.
CHILLI_POWDERY_MILDEW.inspect.2: Check whether leaves are dropping from the plant.
CHILLI_POWDERY_MILDEW.nextStep.1: Note the date you first saw the powdery growth. Published sprays are timed from the first appearance of the symptom.
CHILLI_POWDERY_MILDEW.nextStep.2: Chemical sprays are published for this disease, but this app does not give doses. Contact your nearest KVK, or call the Kisan Call Centre on 1800-180-1551.
CHILLI_POWDERY_MILDEW.symptom.1: A white powdery growth appears on the lower side of the leaves.
CHILLI_POWDERY_MILDEW.symptom.2: Affected leaves are shed, which sharply reduces fruit yield.
COTTON_BACTERIAL_BLIGHT.inspect.1: Look at the underside of leaves for dark green water-soaked patches with straight, angular edges set by the veins.
COTTON_BACTERIAL_BLIGHT.inspect.2: Check whether the veins themselves have turned black.
COTTON_BACTERIAL_BLIGHT.inspect.3: Check stems and fruiting branches for black lesions, cracking, and drooping black twigs.
COTTON_BACTERIAL_BLIGHT.inspect.4: Check bolls for sunken black spots and for early bursting.
COTTON_BACTERIAL_BLIGHT.inspect.5: This disease is favoured by high humidity (around 85 per cent) and by rain followed by bright sunshine. Inspect after such weather.
COTTON_BACTERIAL_BLIGHT.nextStep.1: Remove and destroy infected plant debris.
COTTON_BACTERIAL_BLIGHT.nextStep.2: Rogue out volunteer cotton plants and weed hosts.
COTTON_BACTERIAL_BLIGHT.nextStep.3: Plan crop rotation with non-host crops for the next season.
COTTON_BACTERIAL_BLIGHT.nextStep.4: Seed treatment and sprays are published for this disease, but this app does not give doses. Contact your nearest KVK, or call the Kisan Call Centre on 1800-180-1551.
COTTON_BACTERIAL_BLIGHT.prevention.1: Follow crop rotation with non-host crops.
COTTON_BACTERIAL_BLIGHT.prevention.2: Remove and destroy infected plant debris after harvest — the bacterium survives in dried debris in the soil for several years.
COTTON_BACTERIAL_BLIGHT.prevention.3: Rogue out volunteer cotton plants and weed hosts.
COTTON_BACTERIAL_BLIGHT.symptom.1: Small dark green water-soaked areas appear on the lower surface of the leaves; they become angular because the veins stop them spreading, and can then be seen on both leaf surfaces.
COTTON_BACTERIAL_BLIGHT.symptom.2: The angular spots later turn reddish brown, and the infection spreads into the veins and veinlets.
COTTON_BACTERIAL_BLIGHT.symptom.3: The veins and veinlets blacken, giving a blighted look, and bacterial ooze forms as crusts or scales on the lower leaf surface.
COTTON_BACTERIAL_BLIGHT.symptom.4: Leaves become crinkled and twisted inward, wither, and fall.
COTTON_BACTERIAL_BLIGHT.symptom.5: Dark brown to black lesions form on stems and fruiting branches; the stem cracks and the branch hangs as a dry black twig — the 'black arm' symptom.
COTTON_BACTERIAL_BLIGHT.symptom.6: Bolls show water-soaked lesions that turn into dark black sunken irregular spots; affected bolls shed or burst early, and the lint is stained yellow.
COTTON_BACTERIAL_BLIGHT.symptom.7: In seedlings, small water-soaked lesions appear on the cotyledons and the infection spreads through the leaf stalk to the stem, killing the seedling.
COTTON_CURL_VIRUS.inspect.1: Turn leaves over and look for thickened veins and small leaf-like outgrowths on the underside. These are the signs that separate this from other causes of curling.
COTTON_CURL_VIRUS.inspect.2: Check how many leaves on the plant are curled, and whether the plant's growth has slowed.
COTTON_CURL_VIRUS.inspect.3: Look for whitefly, which carries this virus.
COTTON_CURL_VIRUS.nextStep.1: Remove volunteer perennial cotton plants and other host plants nearby, including wild okra and related plants, which keep the virus alive through the year.
COTTON_CURL_VIRUS.nextStep.2: The virus is carried by whitefly. It is not spread by seed and not spread by touch, so handling plants does not pass it on.
COTTON_CURL_VIRUS.nextStep.3: Contact your nearest KVK, or call the Kisan Call Centre on 1800-180-1551, for local guidance. This app does not give doses.
COTTON_CURL_VIRUS.prevention.1: Adjust the planting date to avoid the peak whitefly period.
COTTON_CURL_VIRUS.prevention.2: Remove volunteer perennial cotton and other host plants around the field.
COTTON_CURL_VIRUS.symptom.2: The leaf veins thicken, and small leaf-like outgrowths (enations) appear on the underside of the leaves.
COTTON_CURL_VIRUS.symptom.3: In severe infection all the leaves are curled, growth is held back, and the plant carries fewer bolls.
COTTON_HEALTHY.inspect.1: No disease signs were found in this check. Keep looking at the crop regularly.
COTTON_HEALTHY.inspect.2: Turn leaves over — bacterial blight patches and leafhopper nymphs both show on the underside first.
COTTON_HEALTHY.inspect.3: Inspect after rain followed by bright sunshine, which favours bacterial blight.
COTTON_HEALTHY.prevention.1: Follow crop rotation with non-host crops.
COTTON_HEALTHY.prevention.2: Remove and destroy infected plant debris.
COTTON_HEALTHY.prevention.3: Rogue out volunteer cotton plants and weed hosts.
COTTON_HEALTHY.prevention.4: Adjust the planting date to avoid the peak whitefly period.
COTTON_HERBICIDE_DAMAGE.inspect.1: Check whether the damage starts on the newest growth at the top of the plant.
COTTON_HERBICIDE_DAMAGE.inspect.2: Look at the shape of the new leaves — long and narrow, twisted, or with odd-looking veins, rather than spotted.
COTTON_HERBICIDE_DAMAGE.inspect.3: This is chemical injury, not an infection. It cannot be told apart from a nutrient problem or a disease from a photograph alone, and the published guidance says even different herbicides are difficult or impossible to tell apart from the symptoms.
COTTON_HERBICIDE_DAMAGE.nextStep.1: This is reported as an observation, not a diagnosis. This app gives no treatment for herbicide injury.
COTTON_HERBICIDE_DAMAGE.nextStep.2: Take an affected plant or a clear photo to your nearest KVK, or call the Kisan Call Centre on 1800-180-1551.
COTTON_HERBICIDE_DAMAGE.symptom.1: Stems and leaf stalks twist and curl.
COTTON_HERBICIDE_DAMAGE.symptom.2: Leaves are out of proportion — unusually long and narrow, which is called strapping — and the leaf veins look abnormal.
COTTON_HERBICIDE_DAMAGE.symptom.3: With some herbicides the plant yellows all over, starting on the newest leaves and spreading to the whole plant.
COTTON_LEAF_HOPPER_JASSIDS.inspect.1: Turn leaves over and look between the veins on the underside for light green, see-through, wingless nymphs. Finding the insect is what tells this apart from leaf reddening caused by other things.
COTTON_LEAF_HOPPER_JASSIDS.inspect.2: Look for small green wedge-shaped adult hoppers on the crop.
COTTON_LEAF_HOPPER_JASSIDS.inspect.3: Count them. The published action level is 50 nymphs or adults across 50 leaves.
COTTON_LEAF_HOPPER_JASSIDS.nextStep.1: Keep the field free of weeds.
COTTON_LEAF_HOPPER_JASSIDS.nextStep.2: Apply nitrogen fertilizer judiciously — do not over-apply.
COTTON_LEAF_HOPPER_JASSIDS.nextStep.3: If counts reach the published action level of 50 hoppers across 50 leaves, contact your nearest KVK, or call the Kisan Call Centre on 1800-180-1551, before spraying. This app does not give doses.
COTTON_LEAF_HOPPER_JASSIDS.prevention.1: Grow hairy (hirsute) cotton varieties, which are less affected.
COTTON_LEAF_HOPPER_JASSIDS.prevention.2: Adopt synchronised sowing with the fields around you.
COTTON_LEAF_HOPPER_JASSIDS.prevention.3: Keep the field free of weeds and apply nitrogen fertilizer judiciously.
COTTON_LEAF_HOPPER_JASSIDS.symptom.1: Leaves curl downward and turn red.
COTTON_LEAF_HOPPER_JASSIDS.symptom.2: Under heavy attack the leaves turn brick red.
COTTON_LEAF_HOPPER_JASSIDS.symptom.3: Plant growth is held back, and plants may die.
COTTON_LEAF_REDDENING.inspect.1: First turn the leaves over and look for leafhoppers on the underside. Leafhopper attack also reddens cotton leaves, and finding the insect changes what the problem is.
COTTON_LEAF_REDDENING.inspect.2: Reddening has many published causes — magnesium shortage, low nitrogen in the leaf or soil, a sudden fall in night temperature, hot days with cold nights, water stress, and waterlogging. A photograph cannot tell which one it is, and more than one may be acting together.
COTTON_LEAF_REDDENING.nextStep.1: This is reported as an observation, not a diagnosis. This app gives no fertilizer or spray recommendation for leaf reddening.
COTTON_LEAF_REDDENING.nextStep.2: Take an affected plant or a clear photo to your nearest KVK, or call the Kisan Call Centre on 1800-180-1551. A soil test will help, since some of the published causes are soil-related.
COTTON_LEAF_REDDENING.symptom.1: The leaves turn red. This is a disorder, not an infection, and the redness is caused by red pigment building up in the leaf.
MAIZE_COMMON_RUST.inspect.1: Rub a pustule with your finger — rust pustules leave a brown powder on the skin.
MAIZE_COMMON_RUST.inspect.2: Check both the upper and lower surfaces of the leaf; the pustules break through on both sides.
MAIZE_COMMON_RUST.inspect.3: This disease is favoured by cool, moist weather, around 15 to 25 degrees Celsius.
MAIZE_COMMON_RUST.nextStep.1: Remove the alternate host weeds (Oxalis species) from around the field — the disease carries over on them.
MAIZE_COMMON_RUST.nextStep.2: Collect the crop remains and destroy them by burning or burying.
MAIZE_COMMON_RUST.nextStep.3: Foliar sprays are published for this disease, but this app does not give doses. Contact your nearest KVK, or call the Kisan Call Centre on 1800-180-1551.
MAIZE_COMMON_RUST.prevention.1: Remove alternate host weeds (Oxalis species) from around the field.
MAIZE_COMMON_RUST.prevention.2: Collect and destroy crop remains after harvest by burning or burying.
MAIZE_COMMON_RUST.symptom.1: Tiny flecks appear on both sides of the leaves.
MAIZE_COMMON_RUST.symptom.2: These become round to elongated cinnamon-brown powdery pustules that break through both leaf surfaces.
MAIZE_COMMON_RUST.symptom.3: As the crop matures, the pustules turn brownish black.
MAIZE_COMMON_RUST.symptom.4: In severe cases the infection spreads to the leaf sheath and other parts.
MAIZE_GRAY_LEAF_SPOT.inspect.1: Start with the lower leaves — this problem shows there first.
MAIZE_GRAY_LEAF_SPOT.inspect.2: Look at the edges of the lesion. If they are straight and stop dead at the veins, that points to grey leaf spot rather than leaf blight, whose lesions are cigar-shaped and taper at the ends.
MAIZE_GRAY_LEAF_SPOT.inspect.3: Look for it around two to three weeks before tasselling, after warm and very humid weather.
MAIZE_GRAY_LEAF_SPOT.nextStep.1: Plan crop rotation and tillage for the next season — both reduce how much of the fungus survives in the residue.
MAIZE_GRAY_LEAF_SPOT.nextStep.2: Ask about resistant hybrids for your area at your nearest KVK, or call the Kisan Call Centre on 1800-180-1551.
MAIZE_GRAY_LEAF_SPOT.prevention.1: Use resistant hybrids where they are available for your area.
MAIZE_GRAY_LEAF_SPOT.prevention.2: Follow crop rotation and tillage, which reduce survival of the fungus in crop residue.
MAIZE_GRAY_LEAF_SPOT.symptom.1: Long, narrow, rectangular lesions, up to about 2 inches long, that start light tan and later turn grey.
MAIZE_GRAY_LEAF_SPOT.symptom.2: The lesions are bounded by the leaf veins, so their edges are straight and they run along the leaf.
MAIZE_GRAY_LEAF_SPOT.symptom.3: Lesions may join together and kill whole leaves.
MAIZE_GRAY_LEAF_SPOT.symptom.4: Symptoms appear on the lower leaves first, about two to three weeks before tasselling.
MAIZE_HEALTHY.inspect.1: No disease signs were found in this check. Keep looking at the crop regularly.
MAIZE_HEALTHY.inspect.2: Start with the lower leaves — leaf blight and grey leaf spot both show there first.
MAIZE_HEALTHY.inspect.3: Check both surfaces of the leaf; rust pustules break through on both sides.
MAIZE_HEALTHY.inspect.4: Check again around two to three weeks before tasselling.
MAIZE_HEALTHY.prevention.1: Burn or bury infected maize stubble after harvest.
MAIZE_HEALTHY.prevention.2: Collect crop remains and destroy them by burning or burying.
MAIZE_HEALTHY.prevention.3: Remove alternate host weeds (Oxalis species) from around the field.
MAIZE_NORTHERN_LEAF_BLIGHT.inspect.2: Look at the lesion shape. Cigar-shaped lesions that taper at both ends point to leaf blight, while rectangular lesions that stop dead at the veins point to grey leaf spot.
MAIZE_NORTHERN_LEAF_BLIGHT.inspect.3: Turn the leaf over and look under a lesion for a dusty black-green fuzz.
MAIZE_NORTHERN_LEAF_BLIGHT.inspect.4: This disease is favoured by wet, humid, cool weather later in the growing season.
MAIZE_NORTHERN_LEAF_BLIGHT.nextStep.1: Burn or bury infected maize stubble — the fungus survives on infected plant debris.
MAIZE_NORTHERN_LEAF_BLIGHT.nextStep.2: Foliar sprays are published for this disease, but this app does not give doses. Contact your nearest KVK, or call the Kisan Call Centre on 1800-180-1551.
MAIZE_NORTHERN_LEAF_BLIGHT.prevention.1: Burn or bury infected maize stubble after harvest.
MAIZE_NORTHERN_LEAF_BLIGHT.symptom.1: Long cigar-shaped lesions, grey-green to tan, appear on the lower leaves.
MAIZE_NORTHERN_LEAF_BLIGHT.symptom.2: The tan lesions are slender and oblong and taper at the ends, ranging from 1 to 6 inches long.
MAIZE_NORTHERN_LEAF_BLIGHT.symptom.3: Lesions run parallel to the leaf margins, join together, and can cover the whole leaf.
MAIZE_NORTHERN_LEAF_BLIGHT.symptom.4: Spores form on the underside of the leaf, and below the lesions the fungus gives a dusty black-green fuzzy appearance.
MAIZE_NORTHERN_LEAF_BLIGHT.symptom.5: Leaves become greyish-green and brittle, resembling leaves killed by frost.
POTATO_EARLY_BLIGHT.inspect.1: Start with the older, lower leaves.
POTATO_EARLY_BLIGHT.inspect.2: Look for the concentric rings in the centre of the spot. This bull's-eye pattern is the identifying feature.
POTATO_EARLY_BLIGHT.inspect.3: Watch the crop from the tuber-bulking stage onwards. Symptoms normally become obvious then and go on developing up to harvest.
POTATO_EARLY_BLIGHT.nextStep.1: Remove and destroy affected plant debris. The spores and fungal threads survive in the soil and in debris for more than 17 months.
POTATO_EARLY_BLIGHT.nextStep.2: Published guidance also lists chemical control for this disease. This app does not give pesticide doses. For a dose, contact your nearest Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) or call the Kisan Call Centre on 1800-180-1551.
POTATO_EARLY_BLIGHT.prevention.1: Select a variety resistant or tolerant to the major pests and diseases, and healthy seed tubers.
POTATO_EARLY_BLIGHT.prevention.2: Keep the crop vigorous with adequate manuring. Poor crop vigour and inadequate manuring are listed as conditions that favour this disease.
POTATO_EARLY_BLIGHT.prevention.3: Follow proper spacing and irrigate properly.
POTATO_EARLY_BLIGHT.symptom.1: Small black lesions appear first, mostly on the older, lower leaves.
POTATO_EARLY_BLIGHT.symptom.2: The spots are brown to black and necrotic, angular to oval, and marked with concentric rings in a bull's-eye pattern.
POTATO_EARLY_BLIGHT.symptom.3: Several spots join up and spread over the whole leaf, and the tissue around the spots may turn yellow.
POTATO_EARLY_BLIGHT.symptom.4: Lesions on the stems look like those on the leaves, and can girdle the plant if they occur near the soil line.
POTATO_EARLY_BLIGHT.symptom.5: The disease occurs both in the hills and in the plains.
POTATO_HEALTHY.inspect.1: Monitor the field at least once a week: the soil, the water, the plants, the pests, the natural enemies and the weather.
POTATO_HEALTHY.inspect.2: Decide what to do from what the field is showing you, and from the balance between pests and their natural enemies. Take direct action when it is needed, such as removing infested plants.
POTATO_HEALTHY.prevention.1: Select a variety resistant or tolerant to the major pests.
POTATO_HEALTHY.prevention.2: Select healthy seed tubers and healthy planting material.
POTATO_HEALTHY.prevention.4: Improve soil health with mulching and green manuring where it applies.
POTATO_HEALTHY.prevention.5: Manage nutrients from a soil test. If the nitrogen dose is too high the crop becomes too succulent and more susceptible to insects and diseases; if it is too low, growth is held back.
POTATO_HEALTHY.prevention.6: Irrigate properly and rotate the crop.
POTATO_LATE_BLIGHT.inspect.1: Turn the leaves over and look for white, flour-like growth on the underside, behind the water-soaked spots.
POTATO_LATE_BLIGHT.inspect.2: Check the stems at the nodes for blackening, and cut open a suspect tuber to look for rusty-brown rot spreading in from the skin.
POTATO_LATE_BLIGHT.inspect.3: Watch the crop closely after cloudy, rainy days when humidity is above 90 per cent and night temperature is around 10 °C. These are the conditions in which this disease spreads.
POTATO_LATE_BLIGHT.nextStep.1: Act at once. This disease can kill infected plants within two or three days.
POTATO_LATE_BLIGHT.nextStep.2: Remove and destroy affected plant material. The pathogen survives in plant debris in the soil, and spreads through the soil and through infected seed tubers.
POTATO_LATE_BLIGHT.nextStep.3: Published guidance also lists chemical control for this disease. This app does not give pesticide doses. For a dose, contact your nearest Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) or call the Kisan Call Centre on 1800-180-1551 straight away.
POTATO_LATE_BLIGHT.prevention.1: Select a variety resistant or tolerant to the major pests and diseases.
POTATO_LATE_BLIGHT.prevention.2: Select healthy seed tubers. Diseased tubers are the main way this disease carries over from one crop to the next.
POTATO_LATE_BLIGHT.prevention.3: Follow proper spacing and irrigate properly.
POTATO_LATE_BLIGHT.symptom.1: Water-soaked spots appear on the leaves, grow larger, turn purple-brown and finally black.
POTATO_LATE_BLIGHT.symptom.2: Affected leaves look blistered, as if scalded with hot water, and then rot and dry out.
POTATO_LATE_BLIGHT.symptom.3: White growth develops on the under surface of the leaves. While the infection is active the underside looks as if it has been dusted with flour.
POTATO_LATE_BLIGHT.symptom.4: The leaf stalks and stems are affected, often at the nodes. The stem breaks there and the plant topples over.
POTATO_LATE_BLIGHT.symptom.5: Affected tubers show purplish-brown spots on the skin and a rusty-brown rot spreading from the surface towards the centre.
POTATO_LATE_BLIGHT.symptom.6: This disease acts very quickly. If it is not controlled, infected plants can die within two or three days.
RICE_BACTERIAL_LEAF_BLIGHT.inspect.1: Look along the leaf margins for wavy, straw-yellow lesions that dry back from the leaf tip.
RICE_BACTERIAL_LEAF_BLIGHT.inspect.2: Look in the early morning for milky or opaque bacterial ooze on young lesions.
RICE_BACTERIAL_LEAF_BLIGHT.inspect.3: The published action thresholds are 2 to 3 infected leaves per square metre for leaf blight, and 2 to 3 affected plants per square metre for the kresek phase.
RICE_BACTERIAL_LEAF_BLIGHT.nextStep.1: Drain the field, except at the flowering stage of the crop.
RICE_BACTERIAL_LEAF_BLIGHT.nextStep.2: Use balanced fertilisation and avoid excess nitrogen, especially late top dressing.
RICE_BACTERIAL_LEAF_BLIGHT.nextStep.3: Remove weeds from the field and the bunds. Weeds are listed as a source of the bacteria.
RICE_BACTERIAL_LEAF_BLIGHT.nextStep.4: Published guidance also lists chemical and antibiotic control for this disease. This app does not give pesticide doses. For a dose, contact your nearest Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) or call the Kisan Call Centre on 1800-180-1551.
RICE_BACTERIAL_LEAF_BLIGHT.prevention.2: Raise the nursery in isolated upland conditions where possible.
RICE_BACTERIAL_LEAF_BLIGHT.prevention.3: Do not clip the tips of the seedlings at transplanting. Clipping is listed as a condition that favours the disease.
RICE_BACTERIAL_LEAF_BLIGHT.symptom.1: Water-soaked, translucent lesions appear near the leaf margin.
RICE_BACTERIAL_LEAF_BLIGHT.symptom.2: The lesions grow in length and width with a wavy margin and turn straw yellow.
RICE_BACTERIAL_LEAF_BLIGHT.symptom.3: Leaves show wavy yellowish-white or golden-yellow dying along the margin and dry back from the tip, curling, while the midrib stays intact.
RICE_BACTERIAL_LEAF_BLIGHT.symptom.4: Milky or opaque dewdrop-like beads of bacteria form on young lesions.
RICE_BACTERIAL_LEAF_BLIGHT.symptom.5: In the kresek phase, seen 1 to 3 weeks after transplanting, seedlings wilt and roll, turn greyish green to yellow, and the plant collapses.
RICE_BLAST.inspect.1: Look at the leaves for spindle-shaped spots with a grey centre and a dark brown edge.
RICE_BLAST.inspect.2: Check the nodes and the neck of the panicle for black or greyish-brown girdling lesions, and see whether any panicles have fallen over.
RICE_BLAST.inspect.3: The published action thresholds are 3 to 5 lesions per leaf for leaf blast, and 2 to 5 neck-infected plants per square metre for neck blast.
RICE_BLAST.nextStep.1: Remove weed hosts from the bunds.
RICE_BLAST.nextStep.2: Do not apply extra nitrogen. Published guidance is to split the nitrogen into three applications.
RICE_BLAST.nextStep.3: Published guidance also lists chemical control for this disease. This app does not give pesticide doses. For a dose, contact your nearest Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) or call the Kisan Call Centre on 1800-180-1551.
RICE_BLAST.prevention.1: Plant a variety resistant to blast. The published guidance calls this the most practical and economical way to control the disease.
RICE_BLAST.prevention.2: Avoid excess nitrogen fertiliser. High nitrogen favours the disease.
RICE_BLAST.prevention.3: Sow disease-free and insect-free pure seed.
RICE_BLAST.symptom.1: Small bluish-green flecks appear on the leaves.
RICE_BLAST.symptom.2: The flecks grow into spindle-shaped spots with a grey or ashy centre and a dark brown margin.
RICE_BLAST.symptom.3: Black lesions form on the nodes and girdle them. Affected nodes may break, and everything above the infected node dies.
RICE_BLAST.symptom.4: Lesions on the neck of the panicle are greyish brown. The neck is girdled and the panicle falls over.
RICE_BLAST.symptom.5: In a severe attack the whole crop looks blasted or burnt.
RICE_BROWN_SPOT.inspect.1: Look on the leaves for oval, dark brown spots with a yellow halo.
RICE_BROWN_SPOT.inspect.2: Check the glumes on the panicle for dark brown or black spots.
RICE_BROWN_SPOT.inspect.3: The published action threshold is 2 to 3 spots per leaf together with 2 to 3 infected plants per square metre.
RICE_BROWN_SPOT.nextStep.1: Do not apply extra nitrogen. The published guidance states that excess nitrogen aggravates this disease.
RICE_BROWN_SPOT.nextStep.2: Published guidance also lists chemical control and seed treatment for this disease. This app does not give pesticide doses. For a dose, contact your nearest Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) or call the Kisan Call Centre on 1800-180-1551.
RICE_BROWN_SPOT.prevention.1: Grow a resistant variety. The published guidance describes this as the most economical means of control.
RICE_BROWN_SPOT.prevention.3: Where the soil is known to be low in plant-available silicon, the published guidance recommends amending it with calcium silicate slag.
RICE_BROWN_SPOT.symptom.1: Minute brown dots appear on the coleoptile, leaf blade, leaf sheath and glume.
RICE_BROWN_SPOT.symptom.2: The dots become cylindrical or oval, dark brown with a yellow halo. Spots measure about 0.5 to 2.0 mm across and join into larger patches.
RICE_BROWN_SPOT.symptom.3: The leaf dries up. A badly affected nursery can be recognised from a distance by its scorched appearance, and seedlings die.
RICE_BROWN_SPOT.symptom.4: Dark brown or black spots also appear on the glumes, discolouring the grain and reducing grain quality and weight.
RICE_NORMAL.inspect.1: Walk the field and observe it weekly, in the morning, preferably before 9 a.m.
RICE_NORMAL.inspect.2: Look at the soil, the water, the plants, the pests, the natural enemies and the weather together, and decide what to do from what the field is showing you.
RICE_NORMAL.inspect.3: The published action thresholds for the common rice diseases are: leaf blast 3 to 5 lesions per leaf; brown spot 2 to 3 spots per leaf with 2 to 3 infected plants per square metre; bacterial leaf blight 2 to 3 infected leaves per square metre; tungro 1 infected plant per square metre.
RICE_NORMAL.prevention.1: Select a suitable resistant or moderately resistant variety.
RICE_NORMAL.prevention.2: Use disease-free and insect-free pure seed, and raise a healthy nursery.
RICE_NORMAL.prevention.3: Plant on time and keep normal spacing of about 30 to 36 hills per square metre, depending on the duration of the variety.
RICE_NORMAL.prevention.4: Use balanced fertiliser and micronutrients as per local recommendations.
RICE_NORMAL.prevention.5: Destroy the leftover nursery, remove weeds from the field and clean the bunds.
RICE_NORMAL.prevention.6: After harvest, flood the field thoroughly and plough it, to destroy the pests that survive in the stubble.
RICE_TUNGRO.inspect.1: Compare the affected plants with their neighbours: look for shorter plants with fewer tillers.
RICE_TUNGRO.inspect.2: Look for green leafhoppers on the plants. The green leafhopper is the insect that carries this virus from plant to plant.
RICE_TUNGRO.inspect.3: The published action threshold is 1 tungro-infected plant per square metre together with 2 green leafhoppers per hill.
RICE_TUNGRO.nextStep.1: Set up light traps to attract the leafhopper vectors and to monitor how many there are.
RICE_TUNGRO.nextStep.3: Published guidance also lists insecticide sprays against the leafhopper vector. This app does not give pesticide doses. For a dose, contact your nearest Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) or call the Kisan Call Centre on 1800-180-1551.
RICE_TUNGRO.prevention.2: Adjust the planting date and keep a fallow period.
RICE_TUNGRO.prevention.3: Rotate the field with pulses or oilseeds.
RICE_TUNGRO.symptom.1: Affected plants are stunted and produce fewer tillers.
RICE_TUNGRO.symptom.2: Leaves turn yellow or orange-yellow and may carry rust-coloured spots.
RICE_TUNGRO.symptom.3: Yellowing starts at the tip of the leaf and may extend down towards the lower part.
RICE_TUNGRO.symptom.4: Young leaves are often mottled with pale green to whitish stripes between the veins.
RICE_TUNGRO.symptom.5: Flowering is delayed. Panicles are small, do not emerge fully, and are mostly sterile or only partly filled.
TOMATO_BACTERIAL_SPOT.inspect.1: Start with the older, lower leaves.
TOMATO_BACTERIAL_SPOT.inspect.2: Check the green fruit for small water-soaked spots that later become sunken and scabby.
TOMATO_BACTERIAL_SPOT.inspect.3: Note the recent weather. Outbreaks are usually traced back to heavy rainstorms in the area.
TOMATO_BACTERIAL_SPOT.nextStep.1: Practise field sanitation. Remove infected plant debris, volunteer tomato plants and solanaceous weeds, where the bacteria survive.
TOMATO_BACTERIAL_SPOT.nextStep.2: Do not save seed from an affected crop. The bacteria contaminate the seed surface and survive there.
TOMATO_BACTERIAL_SPOT.nextStep.3: Published guidance also lists chemical control for this disease. This app does not give pesticide doses. For a dose, contact your nearest Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) or call the Kisan Call Centre on 1800-180-1551.
TOMATO_BACTERIAL_SPOT.prevention.1: Select healthy seeds and healthy seedlings, and a variety resistant or tolerant to the major pests and diseases.
TOMATO_BACTERIAL_SPOT.symptom.1: Small, brown, water-soaked, circular spots with a yellow halo appear on the leaves.
TOMATO_BACTERIAL_SPOT.symptom.2: On older plants the infection is mostly on the older leaves, and can cause serious leaf fall.
TOMATO_BACTERIAL_SPOT.symptom.3: Small, water-soaked spots appear on green fruit. Ripe fruit is not susceptible.
TOMATO_BACTERIAL_SPOT.symptom.4: The centres of the fruit spots become irregular and light brown, with a sunken, rough, scabby surface.
TOMATO_EARLY_BLIGHT.inspect.1: Start with the older, lower leaves. This is where the first lesions appear.
TOMATO_EARLY_BLIGHT.inspect.2: Look for concentric rings in the centre of the spot. This bull's-eye pattern is the identifying feature.
TOMATO_EARLY_BLIGHT.inspect.3: Check the calyx end of the fruit, and the stem near the soil line.
TOMATO_EARLY_BLIGHT.nextStep.1: Practise field sanitation and destroy infected plant debris. The fungus survives in debris in or on the soil for at least a year, and can also be carried on seed.
TOMATO_EARLY_BLIGHT.nextStep.2: Destroy alternate host plants, and give light irrigation.
TOMATO_EARLY_BLIGHT.nextStep.3: Published guidance also lists chemical control for this disease. This app does not give pesticide doses. For a dose, contact your nearest Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) or call the Kisan Call Centre on 1800-180-1551.
TOMATO_EARLY_BLIGHT.prevention.1: Select a variety resistant or tolerant to the major pests and diseases.
TOMATO_EARLY_BLIGHT.prevention.2: Select healthy seeds and healthy seedlings.
TOMATO_EARLY_BLIGHT.prevention.4: Do not apply too much nitrogen fertiliser. If the nitrogen dose is too high the crop becomes too succulent and more susceptible to insects and diseases.
TOMATO_EARLY_BLIGHT.symptom.1: Small black lesions appear first, mostly on the older, lower leaves.
TOMATO_EARLY_BLIGHT.symptom.2: The spots enlarge and show brown concentric rings in a bull's-eye pattern in the centre of the diseased area.
TOMATO_EARLY_BLIGHT.symptom.3: The tissue around the spots may turn yellow. If high temperature and humidity follow, much of the foliage is killed.
TOMATO_EARLY_BLIGHT.symptom.4: Lesions on the stems look like those on the leaves, and can girdle the plant if they occur near the soil line.
TOMATO_EARLY_BLIGHT.symptom.5: The fruit is infected through the calyx or the stem attachment and carries brown concentric rings.
TOMATO_HEALTHY.inspect.1: Start observing the field as soon as the crop is established after transplanting, and then every week.
TOMATO_HEALTHY.inspect.2: Pick five spots at random in the field and five plants at each spot, so that a problem showing up in patches is not missed.
TOMATO_HEALTHY.inspect.3: Turn the leaves over. Mites and whiteflies sit on the underside of the leaf, where they are easy to miss.
TOMATO_HEALTHY.prevention.1: Select a variety resistant or tolerant to the major pests.
TOMATO_HEALTHY.prevention.2: Select healthy seeds and healthy seedlings.
TOMATO_HEALTHY.prevention.4: Improve soil health with mulching and green manuring.
TOMATO_HEALTHY.prevention.5: Manage nutrients from a soil test. If the nitrogen dose is too high the crop becomes too succulent and more susceptible to insects and diseases; if it is too low, growth is held back.
TOMATO_HEALTHY.prevention.6: Irrigate properly and rotate the crop.
TOMATO_LATE_BLIGHT.inspect.1: Look for lesions that are spreading quickly. This disease moves fast in cool nights, warm days and long wet spells from rain or fog.
TOMATO_LATE_BLIGHT.inspect.2: Look for white fungal growth on the affected leaves.
TOMATO_LATE_BLIGHT.inspect.3: Check the fruit for dark brown lesions and soft rot.
TOMATO_LATE_BLIGHT.nextStep.1: Practise field sanitation and destroy affected plants and debris.
TOMATO_LATE_BLIGHT.nextStep.2: Destroy alternate host plants, and give light irrigation.
TOMATO_LATE_BLIGHT.nextStep.3: Published guidance also lists chemical control for this disease. This app does not give pesticide doses. For a dose, contact your nearest Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) or call the Kisan Call Centre on 1800-180-1551.
TOMATO_LATE_BLIGHT.prevention.1: Select a variety resistant or tolerant to the major pests and diseases.
TOMATO_LATE_BLIGHT.prevention.2: Select healthy seeds and healthy seedlings, and follow proper spacing.
TOMATO_LATE_BLIGHT.prevention.3: Do not apply too much nitrogen fertiliser. If the nitrogen dose is too high the crop becomes too succulent and more susceptible to insects and diseases.
TOMATO_LATE_BLIGHT.symptom.1: Water-soaked black lesions appear on the leaves and the stems.
TOMATO_LATE_BLIGHT.symptom.2: The lesions expand rapidly and the whole leaf dies.
TOMATO_LATE_BLIGHT.symptom.3: White fungal growth appears on the leaves.
TOMATO_LATE_BLIGHT.symptom.4: Dark brown lesions form on the fruit, followed by soft rot and breakdown of the fruit.
TOMATO_LEAF_MOLD.inspect.1: Turn the leaf over. The olive-green velvety growth on the underside, directly behind a pale spot on top, is the identifying feature of this disease.
TOMATO_LEAF_MOLD.inspect.2: Start with the older, lower leaves, and check the humidity where the crop is growing. The spores germinate when relative humidity is above 85 per cent.
TOMATO_LEAF_MOLD.nextStep.1: No Indian published guidance for this disease was found for this app, so no treatment is given here. Contact your nearest Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) or call the Kisan Call Centre on 1800-180-1551.
TOMATO_LEAF_MOLD.prevention.1: Select a variety resistant or tolerant to the major pests and diseases, and healthy seeds and seedlings.
TOMATO_LEAF_MOLD.prevention.2: Follow proper spacing and proper irrigation.
TOMATO_LEAF_MOLD.symptom.1: Pale or light green spots appear on the upper surface of the leaf, and later turn yellow or brown.
TOMATO_LEAF_MOLD.symptom.2: On the underside of the leaf, opposite those spots, an olive-green velvety mould growth develops.
TOMATO_LEAF_MOLD.symptom.3: The older, lower leaves are affected first and more severely, and the disease then moves upwards.
TOMATO_LEAF_MOLD.symptom.4: Affected leaf tissue dies and the plant loses leaves.
TOMATO_MOSAIC_VIRUS.inspect.1: Look for a patchwork of light and dark green on the leaf, rather than spots with a definite edge.
TOMATO_MOSAIC_VIRUS.inspect.2: Check the shape of the leaflets: look for puckering, distortion and small, narrow, fern-like leaves.
TOMATO_MOSAIC_VIRUS.nextStep.1: This virus spreads by touch. It travels on clothes, on the hands of working labour, on implements and in plant debris. Handle affected plants last, and wash hands and implements before touching healthy plants.
TOMATO_MOSAIC_VIRUS.nextStep.2: Remove and destroy the infected plants.
TOMATO_MOSAIC_VIRUS.prevention.3: Select healthy seedlings and a variety resistant or tolerant to the major pests and diseases.
TOMATO_MOSAIC_VIRUS.symptom.1: The leaves show light and dark green mottling.
TOMATO_MOSAIC_VIRUS.symptom.2: Young leaves often wilt on sunny days when the plant is first infected.
TOMATO_MOSAIC_VIRUS.symptom.3: The leaflets are distorted, puckered and smaller than normal, and are sometimes so indented that the leaf looks like a fern.
TOMATO_MOSAIC_VIRUS.symptom.4: The affected plant looks stunted, pale green and spindly.
TOMATO_SEPTORIA_LEAF_SPOT.inspect.1: Start with the lower leaves and work upwards.
TOMATO_SEPTORIA_LEAF_SPOT.inspect.2: Look for a grey centre with a dark margin. This distinguishes these spots from the ringed spots of early blight.
TOMATO_SEPTORIA_LEAF_SPOT.inspect.3: Note whether the affected plants are weak. Poor plant vigour from inadequate nutrition is listed as a condition that favours this disease.
TOMATO_SEPTORIA_LEAF_SPOT.nextStep.1: Practise field sanitation and remove infected plant debris and solanaceous weeds, where the fungus survives between crops.
TOMATO_SEPTORIA_LEAF_SPOT.nextStep.2: Pickers can carry this fungus on their hands and clothing. Handle affected plants last, and wash hands and clothes afterwards.
TOMATO_SEPTORIA_LEAF_SPOT.nextStep.3: Published guidance also lists chemical control for this disease. This app does not give pesticide doses. For a dose, contact your nearest Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) or call the Kisan Call Centre on 1800-180-1551.
TOMATO_SEPTORIA_LEAF_SPOT.prevention.1: Select a variety resistant or tolerant to the major pests and diseases, and use healthy seeds and seedlings.
TOMATO_SEPTORIA_LEAF_SPOT.prevention.2: Keep the crop vigorous with nutrient management based on a soil test. Weak plants are the ones this disease attacks.
TOMATO_SEPTORIA_LEAF_SPOT.prevention.3: Follow proper spacing and rotate the crop.
TOMATO_SEPTORIA_LEAF_SPOT.symptom.1: Small, round to irregular spots with a grey centre and a dark margin appear on the leaves.
TOMATO_SEPTORIA_LEAF_SPOT.symptom.2: The spots usually start on the lower leaves and gradually advance upwards.
TOMATO_SEPTORIA_LEAF_SPOT.symptom.3: Spots join together, the leaves are blighted, and affected leaves can be shed completely.
TOMATO_SEPTORIA_LEAF_SPOT.symptom.4: Stems and flowers are sometimes attacked. Fruits are rarely attacked.
TOMATO_SEPTORIA_LEAF_SPOT.symptom.5: Less vigorous plants are usually the ones affected.
TOMATO_SPIDER_MITES.inspect.1: Turn the leaves over. Mites sit on the underside of the leaf. The adult mite is small and red.
TOMATO_SPIDER_MITES.inspect.2: Pick five spots at random in the field, five plants at each spot, and count the young and adult mites on five leaves per plant.
TOMATO_SPIDER_MITES.nextStep.1: Conserve the natural enemies that eat mites: predatory mites, rove beetles, ladybird beetles, lacewings, predatory thrips, anthocorid bugs, mirid bugs and predatory flies.
TOMATO_SPIDER_MITES.nextStep.2: Published guidance also lists chemical control for mites. This app does not give pesticide doses. For a dose, contact your nearest Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) or call the Kisan Call Centre on 1800-180-1551.
TOMATO_SPIDER_MITES.prevention.1: Select a variety resistant or tolerant to the major pests, and healthy seeds and seedlings.
TOMATO_SPIDER_MITES.prevention.2: Follow proper spacing and proper irrigation.
TOMATO_SPIDER_MITES.symptom.1: The affected leaves turn reddish brown and bronzy.
TOMATO_SPIDER_MITES.symptom.2: In a severe infestation there is fine silken webbing on the leaves.
TOMATO_SPIDER_MITES.symptom.4: Flower and fruit formation is affected.
TOMATO_TARGET_SPOT.inspect.1: Look for the concentric rings. Mature leaves are affected more than young leaves, and the disease spreads fastest inside a dense canopy where the leaves stay wet.
TOMATO_TARGET_SPOT.inspect.2: Check the fruit for small sunken brown flecks and for star-shaped cracking.
TOMATO_TARGET_SPOT.nextStep.1: No Indian published guidance for this disease was found for this app, so no treatment is given here. Contact your nearest Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) or call the Kisan Call Centre on 1800-180-1551.
TOMATO_TARGET_SPOT.prevention.1: Select a variety resistant or tolerant to the major pests and diseases, and healthy seeds and seedlings.
TOMATO_TARGET_SPOT.prevention.2: Follow proper spacing and proper irrigation.
TOMATO_TARGET_SPOT.symptom.1: Leaf lesions start as pinpoint dark brown spots.
TOMATO_TARGET_SPOT.symptom.2: The centres become light brown to grey, with dark outer concentric rings, and are sometimes surrounded by yellowing.
TOMATO_TARGET_SPOT.symptom.3: The lesions can join up quickly, blighting the leaf and causing early leaf fall. On leaf stalks and stems the lesions are dark brown and oval.
TOMATO_TARGET_SPOT.symptom.4: On the fruit, damage starts as small, brown, sunken flecks that grow into deeply pitted lesions, and severely affected fruit can crack in an X or star shape as it ripens.
TOMATO_YELLOW_LEAF_CURL_VIRUS.inspect.1: Turn the leaves over and look for whiteflies. The whitefly is the insect that carries this virus from plant to plant.
TOMATO_YELLOW_LEAF_CURL_VIRUS.inspect.2: Check the newest leaves for yellow colouring and curling.
TOMATO_YELLOW_LEAF_CURL_VIRUS.inspect.3: Compare plant height and shape with healthy neighbours: look for short internodes, many side branches and a bushy plant.
TOMATO_YELLOW_LEAF_CURL_VIRUS.nextStep.1: Practise field sanitation. Remove and destroy affected plants, and remove alternate weed hosts.
TOMATO_YELLOW_LEAF_CURL_VIRUS.nextStep.2: Put up yellow sticky traps or cards, about 10 per acre, to reduce the whitefly population.
TOMATO_YELLOW_LEAF_CURL_VIRUS.nextStep.3: Published guidance also lists insecticides against the whitefly vector. This app does not give pesticide doses. For a dose, contact your nearest Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) or call the Kisan Call Centre on 1800-180-1551.
TOMATO_YELLOW_LEAF_CURL_VIRUS.prevention: Raise the nursery under a net with a mesh fine enough to keep whiteflies out.
Take seed only from disease-free, healthy plants.
Remove and destroy infected plants in the nursery. Never transplant a seedling that already shows virus symptoms.
Raise a barrier crop of cereals such as maize, sorghum or bajra around the field.
Remove alternate weed hosts from and around the field.
TOMATO_YELLOW_LEAF_CURL_VIRUS.symptom.2: The leaves roll downwards and become crinkled.
TOMATO_YELLOW_LEAF_CURL_VIRUS.symptom.3: The newly emerging leaves show slight yellow colouring and later curl as well.
TOMATO_YELLOW_LEAF_CURL_VIRUS.symptom.4: Older leaves become leathery and brittle.
TOMATO_YELLOW_LEAF_CURL_VIRUS.symptom.5: The internodes are shortened and the plant produces many lateral branches, giving it a bushy look.
